title: Crew-12 Astronauts Splash Down After Long Mission
summary:
Four astronauts from NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission came home after more than seven months on the International Space Station. Their spacecraft landed in the Pacific Ocean near Los Angeles on Thursday.

They spent 237 days in space, traveled more than 100 million miles, and circled Earth more than 3,792 times. The crew was Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway from NASA, Sophie Adenot from Europe, and Andrey Fedyaev from Russia.

They landed at 8:34 a.m. Pacific time. Rescue teams picked them up by ship. They planned to go to NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

On the station they did science for future Moon and Mars trips, including stem-cell studies and tests for making IV fluids. Meir also did four spacewalks on this mission.
why_it_matters: Learning how crews come home safely helps kids see the teamwork behind space exploration.
